Toyota.description: The largest-selling brand in Pakistan by volume, assembled locally by Indus Motor Company since 1989. Known for resale value and parts availability.

Honda.description: Assembled locally by Honda Atlas Cars Pakistan, with a lineup built around the Civic and City sedans that anchor the compact-executive segment.

Suzuki.description: Pakistan’s highest-volume manufacturer by unit count via Pak Suzuki, dominant in the entry hatchback and light commercial segments.

Kia.description: Assembled by Lucky Motor Corporation, Kia re-entered Pakistan in 2019 and built share quickly in the compact-SUV and crossover segments.

Hyundai.description: Assembled by Hyundai Nishat Motors, with a broad range spanning hatchbacks, sedans and SUVs alongside commercial pickups and vans.

MG.description: Assembled locally by JW Forland/MG affiliates, MG expanded rapidly with SUVs and Pakistan’s first mainstream electric hatchback.

Changan.description: A Chinese manufacturer assembled locally by Master Motors, offering sedans, SUVs and value-focused people movers.

Haval.description: The SUV-focused marque of Great Wall Motors, assembled locally by Sazgar, with a strong push into hybrid crossovers.

Proton.description: A Malaysian brand assembled locally by Al-Haj, offering value sedans and SUVs aimed at the mid-size family segment.

DFSK.description: A Chinese commercial and passenger vehicle brand assembled locally, known for value-oriented seven-seat SUVs.

Prince.description: A locally assembled entry-level hatchback brand aimed squarely at first-time buyers below the 30-lakh mark.

JAC.description: A Chinese manufacturer with a growing local range spanning crossovers to large passenger vans.

FAW.description: One of the earliest Chinese entrants to Pakistan’s market, focused on compact hatchbacks and small MPVs.

United.description: A domestic assembler focused on affordable 800cc hatchbacks for buyers priced out of the used-car market.

Foton.description: Best known internationally for commercial trucks, Foton’s Pakistan lineup includes a value SUV assembled locally.

BAIC.description: A Chinese state-owned manufacturer whose Pakistan lineup is imported and assembled through regional partners, focused on compact SUVs.

Sazgar.description: A domestic assembler that partners with Haval and BAIC, also building its own value-oriented crossovers for the local market.

Regal.description: A newer Chinese entrant assembled locally, focused on compact SUVs and hatchbacks aimed at first-time buyers.

GAC.description: A Guangzhou-based manufacturer that entered Pakistan with imported and locally assembled SUVs and MPVs positioned above the mass-market Chinese brands.

BMW.description: Imported and locally assembled in limited volume by Dewan Motors, BMW’s Pakistan lineup spans sedans and SUVs at the premium end of the market.

Mercedes.description: Assembled locally by Gandhara Motors, Mercedes-Benz anchors the top of Pakistan’s luxury segment across sedans and SUVs.

Audi.description: Sold in Pakistan through independent authorised dealers as fully imported units, with a lineup centred on premium sedans and SUVs.

Porsche.description: A fully imported niche presence in Pakistan through independent dealers, built around its SUV range alongside sports cars.

Volkswagen.description: Reintroduced to Pakistan through Premier Motors with locally assembled and imported models spanning sedans and SUVs.

Jeep.description: An American SUV brand sold in Pakistan through Regal Motors as fully imported units, built around the Wrangler and Grand Cherokee.

Ford.description: Historically assembled locally, Ford’s current Pakistan presence is a small run of imported pickups and SUVs sold through independent dealers.
